lifecycle.note: This classification may inform future work but does not authorize new generation probes.

decision: Create a prompt/control handle registry that distinguishes hard API controls, official-example semantic handles, lower-tier implementation leads, and probabilistic quality hypotheses; do not run new generations yet.
trigger: The executable model graph is now established for the current exact IDs, and the user requested prompt handles/modalities/strategy. Existing official examples and E2E requests contain useful handles, but their causal/quality strength differs.

authorized_by: user requested continued prompt/modality strategy development
rights.scope: classification of existing official examples and project observations

capability.strongest_evidence: E2E for hard controls; D/H for natural-language quality handles
alternative_existing_paths: blindly copy community prompt recipes — rejected because quality evidence is not controlled

intent.user_goal: Give GPT a model-aware prompt language that is useful without confusing examples with proven causal controls.
intent.why_this_action_serves_the_goal: It creates a reusable compiler vocabulary while preserving what still needs probabilistic validation.

cleanup_obligations: promote/demote handle evidence only after controlled tests or source changes
effect.useful_output: prompt/compiler vocabulary with explicit epistemic status

epistemic_review.is_this_a_possibility_graph_edge_or_exec: hard controls may be executable; semantic quality handles remain possibility/probabilistic edges
epistemic_review.what_exact_claim_is_being_tested_or_used: no new causal test; classifies existing evidence
epistemic_review.what_failure_would_falsify: future controlled trials can falsify or bound semantic-handle reliability
epistemic_review.what_failure_would_not_falsify: one poor generation does not prove a semantic handle is universally ineffective
epistemic_review.if_retesting_is_needed_why: only quality/reliability handles need repeated testing when they become load-bearing
